thread:
ada: Heads up — we're seeing repeated inference tail latencies from dedicated-gpu-pool-us-west-2 this morning. Spikes line up with a handful of GPUs going into thermal throttle and fan alarms. svc=redwood-infer-prod-1

infra-bot: alert: node gpu-az3-12 reported NVML events: Xid=79; ECC correctable count increased; PERF state drops; reported 'power limit throttling'

sam: any recent firmware/drivers pushed to that pool? I remember a maintenance push last night for driver 535.86.10.

maria: yep, driver rollout started at 02:10 UTC. rollout batch=3/10 -> this node in batch 3.

ada logs: (pasted from the node)
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE,POWER,FAN,PERF,PCI,ERRORS
GPU 0:
  Temperature: 82 C
  Power Draw: 240 W (PWR cap 200 W)
  Perf State: P12 -> throttling
  Fan Speed: 0 % (fan not responding)
  ECC Errors: Corrected: 12, Uncorrected: 0
  Xid Errors: Xid 79 at 2024-06-05T02:23:12Z
```

kai: fan 0% + high temp + power cap < draw -> HW should have tripped to protect. If fan not spinning, card will throttle and NV driver may emit Xid. Could be failing fan or board-level PSU/EC.

sam: Xid=79 typically indicates a GPU engine hang. Common culprits: thermal, driver, or flaky PCIe link. Also saw a few kernel OOM killer entries in dmesg for the process that manages the NV drivers.

maria: ops note — inference pod logs show repeated token cutoff and 'nvml:context lost' in the runtime: `server: inference loop aborted: NVML_ERROR_LOST`. Clients saw truncated streams. We failed over some requests to smaller models to keep latency under SLA.

ops-oncall: I approve draining gpu-az3-12. Starting drain now: `/usr/local/bin/drain-node --node gpu-az3-12 --pool dedicated-us-west-2 --reason "thermal/fan failure"`

infra-bot: drain job started at 1745123480 by ops-oncall. Current active sessions: 6 -> migrating.

nathan: quick triage checklist I ran:
- `dmesg | grep -i nv` -> shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (79) at ...`
- `ipmitool sdr` -> PSU and temp sensors show inlet_temp=45C, gpu_zone_fan1=0 RPM on node B
- `dmidecode` -> no recent BIOS changes on this rack (last BIOS flash 2023-11)

sam: can someone check BMC logs for SOC/EC events? If the EC is setting a power limit because of a failing fan, that would explain the PWR cap. Also check the IPMI callouts for fan fault.

ada: BMC logs show `FanFault: fan2` and `PSU: overcurrent` ~02:22 UTC. Rebooting the BMC is not stable (it loses LAN).

maria: routing update: gateway policy moved ~20% of traffic off dedicated-us-west-2 to dedicated-us-east-1 and the rest to fallback-small-models in the same region. Cost estimate: +6-10% token spend for the hour while we keep capacity reduced.

kai: action plan proposal:
1) drain and cordon node (in progress).
2) swap card to spare on same host if spares available; otherwise schedule host for reimage + hardware swap.
3) open vendor RMA for the suspected fan/PSU. Include nvml logs, IPMI dumps, BMC logs, driver version.
4) rollback driver 535.86.10 on a canary subset if we reproduce failure on identical cards.
5) add sensor-alert (fan speed==0) to escalate earlier.

ops-oncall: I'll open a hardware ticket now -> HW-TKT-4621. tagging vendor: `@vendor-hw` and support contact.

sam: note — we've seen intermittent reports in eu-west from cards of the same SKU after the driver update but vendor didn't confirm. We should pause the remaining rollout until we confirm.

maria: pausing the driver rollout for remaining batches. Also scaling up dedicated-us-east-1 by 2 nodes to cover capacity for the next 6 hours.

nathan: follow-ups: replace fan module tomorrow in the 9am on-site window, swap PSU if BMC still reports overcurrent after fan swap. I'll attach a short runbook to the ticket.

ada: quick mitigation: enabled aggressive q-cache on the serving runtime to reduce kernel invocations -> decreased retries by ~30% while the node drained.

sam: possible root causes we should track in the ticket: hardware failure (fan/PSU), driver regression (535.86.10), BMC firmware edge case, thermal dust/clog.

kai: risk note: if multiple cards in a rack show zero RPM fans we might be looking at a shared power rail / chassis fan controller failure. Check chassis-level fan controller and the presence of any correlated events across siblings.

maria: agreed. I'll run a correlation query across `gpu-az3-*` nodes for FanFault/IPMI errors between 02:00-03:00 UTC.

ops-oncall: drain complete: all sessions migrated, node cordoned. Scheduling host out-of-service. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident logged in #incidents with id INC-20240605-89 and summary "GPU thermal + fan failures causing Xid 79 and inference truncation — drained node gpu-az3-12, paused driver rollout"

ada: will follow up with the vendor RMA, hardware swap checklist, and a postmortem draft once we have BMC dumps. Thanks all.

sam: one more ask — add a metric for 'fan_rpm==0 && temp>75' to alert earlier. I can draft a rule.

maria: creating a Grafana alert now and will route to #pagerduty-gpu on-call.

nathan: noted for the postmortem: include cost delta from fallback routing, number of truncated requests, and estimated MTTR.

ada: ok — closing the loop here. If anyone observes more Xid 79 on other nodes, ping `@ops-oncall` immediately.

(Conversation ends)
